1.1: Sha’ul, a prisoner of Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and Timotiyos the brother, to Pilĕymon our beloved one and fellow worker,
1.2: and Apphia our sister, and Arḵippos our fellow soldier, and the assembly at your house:
1.3: Favor to you and peace from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Father and the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.4: I always thank my Elohim when I mention you in my prayers,
1.5: hearing of your love and the belief which you have toward the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and toward all the qodeshim,
1.6: so that the sharing of your belief might become working in the knowledge of all the good which is in you toward Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
1.7: For we have much joy and encouragement in your love, because the tender affections of the qodeshim have been refreshed by you, brother.
1.8: Therefore, although I have much boldness in Mashiaḥ to command you what is fitting,
1.9: because of love, I rather appeal - being such a one as Sha’ul, the aged, and now also a prisoner of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ -
1.10: I appeal to you for my child Onĕsimos, whom I brought forth while in my chains,
1.11: who formerly was of no use to you, but now is of good use to you and to me,
1.12: whom I sent back to you, and receive him, that is, my own tender affections,
1.13: whom I wanted to keep with me, that on your behalf he might serve me in my chains for the Good News.
1.14: But without your opinion I wanted to do naught, so that your good deed should not be by way of necessity, but voluntary.
1.15: For he departed for a while, possibly because of this, so that you might have him back forever,
1.16: no longer as a slave but more than a slave, as a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Aḏon.
1.17: So, if you regard me as your partner, receive him as you would me.
1.18: But if he has wronged you or owes you whatever, put that on my account.
1.19: I, Sha’ul, write with my own hand. I shall repay - not to mention to you that you indeed owe yourself to me also.
1.20: Yes, brother, let me derive pleasure from you in the Aḏon, refresh my tender affections in the Aḏon.
1.21: Trusting in your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you shall do even more than I say.
1.22: And at the same time also prepare a place for me to stay, for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given to you.
1.23: Epaphras, fellow prisoner of me in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, greets you,
1.24: Markos, Aristarḵos, Dĕmas, Lukas, my fellow workers.
1.25: The favor of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Mashiaḥ be with your spirit. Amĕn.
